description: A repeatable operating method for building and scaling reliable AI-Augmented capability.

stages.name: Diagnose
stages.purpose: Understand the current work, capability, risks, and desired human outcome.
stages.exitGate: The team can explain the problem, desired outcome, affected people, and material risks.
stages.example: A university maps how a student advising request moves from intake to decision and identifies where AI could improve preparation without replacing advisor judgment.

stages.name: Activate
stages.purpose: Create the shared intent, capability, and conditions needed to begin responsible change.
stages.exitGate: The people doing the work understand the intended outcome, their responsibilities, and the first safe action.
stages.example: A finance team agrees on a bounded drafting use case, assigns a reviewer, and defines what information must remain protected.

stages.name: Controls
stages.purpose: Set the safeguards, review practices, and accountability needed for reliable work.
stages.exitGate: The workflow has proportionate controls and a named human owner for consequential decisions.
stages.example: A legal team defines which draft sections require source verification and attorney approval before client delivery.

stages.name: Execute
stages.purpose: Put the AI-supported workflow into practice and learn from real work.
stages.exitGate: The workflow can be performed consistently with the required review and ownership visible.
stages.example: A teacher uses an AI-supported rubric drafting workflow, checks the result against learning goals, and edits it before sharing it with students.

stages.name: Measure
stages.purpose: Evaluate whether the AI-supported work improves outcomes and preserves trust.
activities: Compare results with the intended outcome
outputs: Decision to improve, pause, or expand
stages.exitGate: The team has evidence about value, quality, risk, and the changes required before expansion.
stages.example: An operations group compares turnaround time and correction rates before and after introducing an AI-supported intake workflow.

stages.name: Scale
stages.purpose: Extend proven capability while adapting governance, training, and support to the new scope.
stages.exitGate: The capability can expand without losing outcome quality, contextual judgment, ownership, or trust.
stages.example: A university extends a reviewed AI workflow from one advising team to multiple campuses with shared standards and local accountability.
